asA: verifier at the TEST stage, with the reviewer reading the result
iWant: a tool that fails any bound test reaching around the app entry, mocking an internal module, or relying on a silently defaulted logger, emitter or sender
soThat: a green suite means production as wired does what the criteria say
title: The verifier runs the structural check over the bound tests of the touched criteria

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given a fixture project whose rcf/test-strength.json declares entry [{"kind": "bin", "path": "bin/app.js"}] and harness ["test/_harness/**"], and whose AC-101-1 is bound to test/rcf/a.test.js importing only node:test, node:assert and test/_harness/run.js (which spawns bin/app.js), with a symbol-level Code Node whose mutants all fail that test, when rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1 runs, then it exits 0 and stdout is "test-strength: PASS 1 criteria at <h7>: structural 1/1, mutants killed 3/3 (timeout 0, notApplicable 0)" (or killed 2/2 with notApplicable 1 when call removal finds no call site).

[failure] Given the same fixture with test/rcf/a.test.js also importing src/store.js (a product file that is not the entry), when rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1 runs, then it exits 4 and stdout is "test-strength: FAIL 1 of 1 criteria at <h7>: AC-101-1 imports src/store.js (not the app entry or the harness)".

[failure] Given the same fixture with test/rcf/a.test.js calling mock.module("../../src/mailer.js", ...) and rcf/test-strength.json declaring edge ["node:https"], the verb exits 4 with "AC-101-1 mocks ../../src/mailer.js (not a declared edge)"; a mock.module("node:https", ...) in the same test is not a finding.

[failure] Given a Code Node src/notify.js#makeNotifier implementing AC-101-1 whose function is makeNotifier({ sender = consoleSender } = {}), when rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1 runs, then it exits 4 with "AC-101-1 silent default sender in src/notify.js#makeNotifier"; a parameter named sender with no default is not a finding.

[edge] Given a fixture project with no rcf/test-strength.json, rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1 exits 2 with stderr "test-strength: no rcf/test-strength.json; declare entry and harness"; given no --acs, no --fbs and no REVIEW verdict reachable from HEAD, it exits 2 with "test-strength: no scope; pass --acs or --fbs, or record a REVIEW verdict"; given --acs AC-999-1 it exits 2 naming AC-999-1.

[must-not] The structural check never executes a test, the entry or any product module: it reads bound test files and Code Node sources as text, so a bound test file that would throw on import still yields its import findings, and a structural-only failure is reported without running a single mutant.

[edge] Given --acs AC-101-1,AC-101-2 where AC-101-1's bound test imports src/store.js and AC-101-2 passes the structural check, rcf audit test-strength runs the structural check for both first, runs mutants for AC-101-2 only, exits 4 naming AC-101-1's imports finding, and --json lists mutants for AC-101-2 and none for AC-101-1.

[failure] Given a bound test file test/rcf/a.test.ts, or a Code Node on src/x.ts, rcf audit test-strength exits 2 with stderr "test-strength: <path> is not a supported source (JavaScript ESM or CommonJS)" and runs no mutant; bound tests and Code Nodes in .js, .mjs and .cjs files are read.
acceptanceCriteria.supersessionNote: Retired 2026-10-29 (the stage-keeper's retire-and-succeed ruling on AC-19901-8, round D RC-46 DEFINE, round A ruling 5: retired and succeeded, never reworded): RC-46 reads .ts, .tsx and .vue bound tests and Code Nodes (US-19904), and a file the audit cannot read is reported per criterion as BLOCKED (stage-keeper ruling Q2 (a)), so the whole-run exit 2 for every non-JavaScript source no longer holds; AC-19901-9 states the 0.39.0 rule.

acceptanceCriteria.description: [failure] Given AC-101-1 bound to a test file `test/rcf/a.test.py`, or claiming a symbol-level Code Node `src/x.py#run`, a file that is none of .js, .mjs, .cjs, .ts, .mts, .cts, .tsx, .jsx or .vue, and AC-101-2 bound to a passing `.js` test over a symbol-level `.js` Code Node, when `rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1,AC-101-2` runs, then AC-101-1 is reported per criterion as BLOCKED (stage-keeper ruling Q2 (a)): its criterion in the TestStrengthReport carries `result` "blocked", `reason` "TEST_STRENGTH_UNSUPPORTED" and a `detail` `<file>:<line>:<col>: <construct>` for the first unreadable construct of each file, a criterion with several unreadable files listing each file's first construct in bound order, joined by "; " (a bound test file or a symbol-level Code Node file strip mode refuses reads `<file>:<line>:<col>: non-erasable TypeScript syntax (<construct>)`, the one wording AC-19904-7 uses, and an entry the strip view cannot parse exits 2 "entry point unreadable" with the same detail). `<line>` and `<col>` are 1-based and place the first character of the construct in the file as committed: `<line>` counts the line breaks before it, a line break being CRLF, a lone CR or LF (U+2028 and U+2029 are not line breaks); `<col>` counts UTF-16 code units from the start of that line, a tab, a form feed, a vertical tab, a byte order mark and a combining mark one unit each and a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane two. For a construct strip mode refuses or a syntax error, that is the construct node's refusal places, whatever characters precede it on the line; when the input ends inside a construct (an unclosed bracket, string, template literal or block comment), it is where the innermost such construct opens. When node names a line and no column (the input ends with nothing open), the refusal is placed at that line, column 1. A `.vue` file's position counts in the `.vue` file, and a `.tsx` or `.jsx` file's JSX scan failure by the same rule. The run continues for AC-101-2, which is judged as before (pass); no stderr line reads "is not a supported source"; and the run exits 5, the BLOCKED exit, its summary line the BLOCKED line AC-19904-7 rules. Given instead AC-101-1 blocked by the same `.py` bound test and AC-101-2 failing the structural check (bound to a test also importing `src/store.js`), the fail verdict and its exit code win: the run exits 4, the FAIL exit, with the FAIL line naming AC-101-2's finding, and the summary line still counts the blocked criteria and lists their ids, the FAIL line ending ", blocked 1: " with AC-101-1 and its file. Exit 2 covers every whole-run failure: the audit's own inputs unreadable (`rcf/test-strength.json`, the entry point, an entry the strip view cannot parse included, or a `runners` entry), a bound test not committed, a runner that cannot run the bound tests or reports no bound test, and an ambiguous leaf; under the exit precedence TAC-4155 states (2 over 4 over 5 over 0) a blocked criterion beside a whole-run failure still exits 2. For the unsupported-file case a whole-run exit 2 remains only when the audit's own inputs are unreadable: a `runners` entry whose `kind` is none of nodeTest, vitest or playwright exits 2 with a stderr line starting "test-strength: malformed rcf/test-strength.json". Bound tests and symbol-level Code Nodes in .js, .mjs and .cjs files are read, and in .ts, .tsx and .vue files as US-19904 rules; .jsx files are read through the same JSX scanner as .tsx and are never blocked for being JSX, and .mts and .cts files are read as .ts (the stage-keeper's ruling F5). This criterion covers bound test files and symbol-level Code Nodes only: a file-level Code Node on a non-code file keeps fileBlank (AC-19902-8).
